correctness.description:
Test `test_bucket_created` passes: Test 1: Verify S3 bucket was created
Purpose: Confirms bucket creation logic worked

Test `test_sqs_queue_exists` passes: Test 2: Verify prerequisite SQS queue exists
Purpose: Validates environment setup

Test `test_bucket_notification_to_sqs_configured` passes: Test 3: Verify S3 → SQS notification setup
Purpose: Validates notification wiring

Test `test_queue_policy_allows_s3` passes: Test 4: Verify SQS queue has policy allowing S3
Purpose: Ensures permission configuration is correct

Test `test_file_uploaded_to_correct_location` passes: Test 5: Verify test file was uploaded
Purpose: Confirms upload step completed

Test `test_sqs_message_received` passes: Test 6a: Verify message was processed by checking output file exists
Purpose: Validates that the solution script successfully processed an SQS message

This test confirms that at least one message was received and processed.

Test `test_no_duplicate_messages_in_queue` passes: Test 6b: Verify no duplicate or unprocessed messages remain in queue
Purpose: Ensures clean message processing without duplicates

After the solution runs, the queue should be empty (or only contain test events).
This validates that messages are properly consumed and not left in the queue.

Test `test_output_file_created` passes: Test 7: Verify output file was created with event details
Purpose: Validates message content was correctly extracted and stored

Test `test_end_to_end_notification_with_new_upload` passes: Test 8: Complete end-to-end validation with a new file upload
Purpose: Validates that the notification configuration works independently

This test uploads a new file and verifies a message is received in the queue,
confirming that the S3-to-SQS notification pipeline is truly functional
and not just relying on pre-existing messages.

functional.description: The solution connects to LocalStack endpoints for both S3 and SQS ('http://localhost:4566')
functional.rationale: Ensures the solution interacts with the local emulation environment instead of production AWS services.

functional.description: The solution configures the S3 bucket notification to send events to the specified SQS queue
functional.rationale: Connecting S3 to SQS via notifications is the primary functional requirement.

functional.description: The solution sets an SQS access policy allowing 's3:SendMessage' from the source bucket
functional.rationale: Explicit permissions are required for S3 to publish messages to the SQS queue.

robustness.description: The solution checks if the S3 bucket already exists before attempting to create it
robustness.rationale: Prevents errors when running the script multiple times (idempotency).

robustness.description: The solution explicitly deletes SQS messages after processing
robustness.rationale: Failure to delete messages results in them returning to the queue after the visibility timeout, causing duplicate processing.

robustness.description: The solution uses SQS long polling (WaitTimeSeconds > 0) to efficiently retrieve messages
robustness.rationale: Long polling reduces empty responses and API costs while improving message delivery latency.

robustness.description: The solution handles or filters unexpected message structures (e.g., S3 TestEvents) gracefully
robustness.rationale: S3 sends a test event upon configuration; the script should not crash or misinterpret this event.
